Medline, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and Google Scholar were searched up to September 15, 2023 for articles reporting the RPE atrophy growth rate in treatment-naïve eyes with geographic atrophy (GA), Stargardt disease (STGD1), Best disease, pseudoxanthoma elasticum (PXE), central areolar choroidal dystrophy (CACD), or pattern dystrophies with no previous or current macular neovascularization and a minimum follow-up time of 12 months. Meta-analyses determined mean RPE atrophy growth rates per disease, imaging modality (fundus autofluorescence [FAF], optical coherence tomography [OCT], or color fundus photography [CFP]) and metric (mm2/y or mm/y). The Newcastle-Ottawa scale and the Cochrane Risk-of-Bias tool assessed the risk of bias, and funnel plots were used to evaluate small-study effects.

Results

From 4354 publications, 85 were included for meta-analysis: 69 studies (7815 eyes) on GA, 15 (1367 eyes) on STGD1, and one on both. Two studies on PXE were only eligible for review. No studies for other diseases met our eligibility criteria. The overall mean RPE atrophy growth rate for GA using FAF was 1.65 mm2/y (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.49-1.81) and 0.35 mm/y (95% CI, 0.28-0.41); using OCT, it was 1.46 mm2/y (95% CI, 1.28-1.64) and 0.34 mm/y (95% CI, 0.28-0.40); and on CFP it was 1.76 mm2/y (95% CI, 1.56-1.97) and 0.30 mm/y (95% CI, 0.28-0.31). For STGD1, using FAF it was 1.0 mm2/y (95% CI, 0.77-1.23) and 0.20 mm/y (95% CI, 0.17-0.23); on OCT, it was 0.80 mm2/y (95% CI, 0.72-0.88). No studies on STGD1 reported the growth rate with other imaging modalities or metrics. Growth rates in GA were faster than in STGD1 (p < .05). A larger baseline area of atrophy was generally associated with faster growth rates.

Conclusions

The RPE atrophy growth rate in GA is faster than in STGD1 but with great variation between studies and imaging modalities. Limited information was available for other macular IRD, suggesting further research is needed.

records.title: SURGICAL DRAINAGE METHODS DURING PARS PLANA VITRECTOMY FOR RHEGMATOGENOUS RETINAL DETACHMENT: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: SURGICAL DRAINAGE METHODS DURING PARS PLANA VITRECTOMY FOR RHEGMATOGENOUS RETINAL DETACHMENT: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To assess efficacy and safety outcomes of subretinal fluid drainage methods during pars plana vitrectomy for rhegmatogenous retinal detachment.

Methods

A systematic search strategy was conducted for studies published between January 2000 and October 2022. Included studies reported on either the safety or efficacy of two or more drainage methods during pars plana vitrectomy for patients with rhegmatogenous retinal detachment.

Results

Two randomized and five observational studies consisting of 1,524 eyes were included. Best-corrected visual acuity at the last study observation and primary reattachment rates were similar across groups. A significantly lower risk of epiretinal membrane formation was associated with draining subretinal fluid through preexisting retinal breaks (risk ratio = 0.70, 95% confidence interval = [0.60, 0.83], P = <0.01, I 2 = 0%) or with perfluorocarbon liquid (risk ratios = 0.70, 95% confidence interval = [0.59, 0.83], P = <0.01, I 2 = 0%) compared with posterior retinotomy. The risk of an abnormal foveal contour was significantly greater in perfluorocarbon liquid-treated eyes relative to posterior retinotomy (risk ratios = 1.56, 95% confidence interval = [1.13, 2.17], P = <0.01, I 2 = 0%).

Conclusion

No significant differences were observed in the final best-corrected visual acuity at the last study observation and primary reattachment rates across different drainage methods. There remains limited information on the topic, so future research is warranted.

records.title: Pars Plana Vitrectomy With Silicone Oil or Gas Tamponade for Uncomplicated Retinal Detachment: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Pars Plana Vitrectomy With Silicone Oil or Gas Tamponade for Uncomplicated Retinal Detachment: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare the efficacy and safety of pars plana vitrectomy (PPV) with silicone oil compared to gas tamponade for uncomplicated rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD).

Design

Systematic review and meta-analysis.

Methods

A systematic literature search was conducted on Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from January 2000 to September 2023 for comparative studies evaluating the efficacy and safety of PPV with either silicone oil or gas tamponade in the setting of uncomplicated RRD. Our primary outcome was best-corrected visual acuity at the last study observation. Secondary outcomes included the rates of retinal reattachment, retinal thickness, and the incidence of adverse events. We performed a meta-analysis using a random-effects model.

Results

Nine observational studies reporting on 491 RRD eyes were included. The mean best-corrected visual acuity at the last study observation was significantly better in the gas tamponade group than in the silicone oil group (weighted mean difference [WMD] = 0.17 logMAR, 95% confidence interval [CI] = [0.06, 0.27], P = .002). Rates of primary retinal reattachment were similar between the silicone oil and gas tamponade groups (P = .89). The ganglion cell layer was significantly thinner in the silicone oil group compared to the gas tamponade group (WMD =-3.70 µm, 95% CI = [-5.87, -1.53, P = .0008), as was the inner plexiform layer (WMD = -2.45, 95% CI = [-4.50, -0.40], P = .02) and outer nuclear layer (WMD = -11.74 µm, 95% CI = [-18.39, -5.10], P = .0005).

Conclusions

PPV with gas tamponade was associated with better functional outcomes compared to PPV with silicone oil, although both tamponades yielded comparable primary reattachment rates. The absence of randomized trials and the potential for selection bias underscore the importance of further investigation in diverse patient populations.

records.title: Accuracy of six contemporary toric formulas: analysis of 6753 eyes.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Accuracy of six contemporary toric formulas: analysis of 6753 eyes.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare the predictive accuracy of 4 toric intraocular lens (IOL) formulas (Barrett, EVO, Hoffer QST, and Kane) integrated in the ESCRS calculator. Barrett and EVO were tested with measured (Barrett M and EVO M) and predicted (Barrett P and EVO P) posterior corneal curvature.

Setting

Multiple surgical centers in the United States.

Design

Retrospective database study.

Methods

6753 eyes implanted with nontoric IOLs were analyzed. Preoperative biometry, including posterior corneal curvature, was obtained using the IOLMaster 700. Predicted residual astigmatism was calculated through the proprietary websites of the 4 toric formulas integrated into the ESCRS IOL power calculator. Primary endpoints were the mean vector magnitude error and proportions of eyes with vector magnitude prediction errors ≤0.50 diopters (D).

Results

Kane demonstrated the lowest mean vector magnitude prediction error (0.537 D), significantly lower than EVO P (0.561 D), EVO M (0.57 D), Barrett M (0.579 D), Barrett P (0.583 D), and Hoffer QST (0.622 D) (all P < .001). This result was consistent in with-the-rule, against-the-rule, and oblique subgroups. Kane also achieved the highest proportion of eyes with prediction error ≤0.50 D ( P < .001). For all formulas, centroid values were significantly different from zero. The Kane formula showed the lowest total variances, significantly lower than all other formulas ( P < .001).

Conclusions

The Kane formula showed statistically superior predictive accuracy with the lowest errors and variances and the highest proportion of eyes within 0.50 D. However, differences among formulas were small, and their clinical relevance for toric IOL outcomes remains uncertain.

records.title: Baseline OCT Biomarkers Predicting Visual Outcomes in Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration: A Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Baseline OCT Biomarkers Predicting Visual Outcomes in Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration: A Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Topic

To determine the effect estimates and certainty of evidence for baseline OCT biomarkers predicting visual acuity (VA) and changes in VA from baseline at 6, 12, and 24 months after anti-vascular endothelial growth factor therapy for neovascular age-related macular degeneration.

Clinical relevance

Understanding the prognostic utility of biomarkers can improve treatment decisions.

Methods

Results were reported in ETDRS letters. Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluations (GRADE) guidelines for prognostic studies informed certainty of evidence. Results were interpreted using a 5-letter minimally important difference.

Results

Twenty-nine reports (8863 eyes) evaluating 80 biomarkers were included. Two biomarkers predicted better VA at 12 months with a low-certainty: the presence of an intact external limiting membrane (+14.0; 95% confidence interval [CI], +3.1 to +24.8) and the presence of an intact ellipsoid zone (+6.8; 95% CI, +2.8 to +10.8). Three biomarkers predicted worse VA at 12 months with a low certainty; the presence of intraretinal fluid (IRF; -5.6; 95% CI, -9.7 to -1.5), the presence of IRF in the foveal center point (-7.4; 95% CI, -10.1 to -4.7), and the presence of subretinal hyperreflective material (-8.7; 95% CI, -19.0 to 1.6). No other biomarker predicted an effect size that crossed the minimally important difference. However, noteworthy results occurred when interpreting biomarkers with statistically significant findings relative to a threshold of 0 letters and moderate certainty: the presence of a pigment epithelial detachment, geographic atrophy (GA), and both IRF and subretinal fluid (SRF) predicted reduced vision at 12 months. The presence of SRF predicted a positive change in VA at 12 months. The absence of a posterior vitreous detachment predicted a negative change in VA at 12 months. Finally, the presence of IRF in the central 1 mm, retinal pigment epithelial elevation, and GA predicted negative changes in VA at 24 months.

Discussion

With low-certainty evidence, the baseline presence of an intact external limiting membrane and ellipsoid zone predicted better VA at 12 months, and the presence of IRF, IRF in the foveal center point, and subretinal hyperreflective material predicted worse VA at 12 months. Improved standardization in biomarker classification and control of confounding variables is needed.

Financial disclosure(s)

Proprietary or commercial disclosure may be found in the Footnotes and Disclosures at the end of this article.

records.title: Transformation of the extracellular matrix during uveal melanoma development, progression, and at the hepatic metastatic niche.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Transformation of the extracellular matrix during uveal melanoma development, progression, and at the hepatic metastatic niche.
content.abstract: The tumour microenvironment comprising tumour cells, immune infiltrates, stromal components, and the extracellular matrix (ECM) plays a central role in cancer biology, modulating key hallmarks, such as proliferation, immune evasion, and metastasis. The ECM is a dynamic network of collagens, elastin, glycoproteins, and proteoglycans and emerging evidence highlights its role in tumour progression, with loss of matrix organisation altering tumour cell behaviour through both pro- and anti-tumourigenic mechanisms. Uveal melanoma (UM), the most common primary intraocular malignancy in adults, carries a poor prognosis due to its propensity for hepatic metastasis and limited therapeutic options. The uveal tract, comprising the choroid, ciliary body, and iris, relies on highly specialised ECM architectures, and we describe in this review how they support nutrient exchange, lens accommodation, and light regulation while mediating essential biochemical and biomechanical signalling. Understanding this baseline ECM is essential for interpreting the pathological matrix remodelling that occurs in UM. We describe marked compositional differences in ECM between low- and high-metastatic risk primary UM, revealing key mechanisms of tumour progression, including upregulation of structural collagens, fibronectin, laminins, and ECM-remodelling enzymes that activate oncogenic signalling pathways enhancing proliferation, invasion, and metastatic competence. We also explore the hepatic metastatic niche, where stellate cell-driven ECM remodelling promotes a fibrotic, immune-restrictive microenvironment that limits therapeutic efficacy. Finally, we discuss experimental constraints limiting ECM research and highlight advances in decellularised scaffolds, three-dimensional culture systems, and multi-omics technologies to dissect tumour-matrix interactions and uncover ECM-targeted therapeutic vulnerabilities with the potential to improve UM's poor clinical outcomes.

records.title: Assessing the Fragility of Statistically Significant Outcomes in Randomized Controlled Trials of Minimally Invasive Glaucoma Surgery (MIGS).

content.title: Assessing the Fragility of Statistically Significant Outcomes in Randomized Controlled Trials of Minimally Invasive Glaucoma Surgery (MIGS).
content.abstract:
Topic

Minimally invasive glaucoma surgery (MIGS) has been widely adopted as a surgical option for glaucoma, yet concerns remain regarding the robustness of the evidence supporting many procedures. The fragility index (FI) and fragility quotient (FQ) provide complementary measures to traditional p values by quantifying how dependent statistically significant results are on a small number of outcome events.

Clinical relevance

Understanding the statistical fragility of MIGS trials is important for clinicians, guideline developers, and policymakers when interpreting reported efficacy and safety outcomes, particularly in a field characterised by small trials, heterogeneous endpoints, and commercially sensitive interventions.

Methods

A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines and registered on PROSPERO. Electronic databases were searched from inception to August 1, 2025, to identify randomized controlled trials evaluating MIGS procedures in patients with glaucoma. Trials reporting at least one statistically significant binary outcome with sufficient raw data were included. The FI was calculated using iterative Fisher exact testing, and the FQ was derived by normalizing FI to total sample size. Risk of bias was assessed using the Revised Cochrane Risk of Bias Tool (RoB 2.0).

Results

Sixteen randomized controlled trials encompassing 4,562 participants met inclusion criteria. The median sample size was 236.5 (interquartile range [IQR], 88-511), with a median follow-up of 24 months. The mean FI was 9.4 ± 10.0 and the mean FQ was 0.031 ± 0.025, indicating that approximately 3% of participants would require a different outcome to render results non-significant. Three trials (18.8%) had an FI of zero. In six studies (37.5%), the FI was less than or equal to the number of participants lost to follow-up, suggesting vulnerability to attrition bias. Fragility varied across device categories, with larger multicenter trials demonstrating higher FI values but consistently low FQ values.

Conclusion

Statistically significant outcomes in RCTs of MIGS exhibit variable statistical robustness when assessed using fragility metrics, often due to small numbers of events. These findings highlight the need for cautious interpretation of reported significance and support the incorporation of fragility metrics alongside conventional statistical measures when appraising the MIGS evidence base.

records.title: An Agentic AI Workflow for Automated Macular Hole Diagnosis and Structured Report Generation.

content.title: An Agentic AI Workflow for Automated Macular Hole Diagnosis and Structured Report Generation.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Current AI models for optical coherence tomography (OCT) primarily focus on diagnosis as a standalone task. We developed and validated an end-to-end agentic AI workflow that integrates automated macular hole (MH) diagnosis from OCT images with structured patient-friendly report generation.

Methods

The proposed sequential workflow coordinated by a workflow orchestration agent consisted of an image diagnosis stage and a language generation step. The OCT version of RETFound, a self-supervised retinal foundation model, was fine-tuned for binary classification of macular OCT scans as MH or normal macula. Training, validation, and internal testing were performed using multiple public OCT datasets with patient-level stratified splitting, followed by external validation on two independent datasets. The performance of the fine-tuned foundation model was evaluated using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC AUC). For each new OCT image, the AI agent used the trained RETFound model to classify the image, received the diagnostic output, incorporated it into a structured prompt, and called the large language model (GPT-4) to generate the clinical report.

Results

On the internal test set (n = 180), the model achieved an accuracy of 100% (95% confidence interval (CI), 97.9-100%) with an AUC of 1.00. On external validation (n = 1014), accuracy was 98.8% (95% CI 97.9-99.3%), sensitivity was 97.9% (95% CI 96.3-98.8%), specificity was 100% (95% CI 99.2-100.0%), and AUC was 0.999 (95% CI 0.998-1.000). Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) analysis showed that predictions were driven by relevant retinal regions, particularly the macular hole and adjacent layers. The end-to-end agentic AI workflow generated concise and standardized patient-friendly reports for all samples, without the language model influencing diagnostic decisions.

Conclusions

This study demonstrates the feasibility of an end-to-end AI workflow coordinated by a workflow orchestration agent for robust OCT-based MH diagnosis with a large language model for structured report generation. By separating image-based diagnosis from language generation, this approach offers a practical and scalable solution for virtual vitreoretinal clinics.

records.title: Early Diagnosis and Prognosis of Corneal and Ocular Surface Pathologies Using Artificial Intelligence: A State-of-the-art Review.

content.title: Early Diagnosis and Prognosis of Corneal and Ocular Surface Pathologies Using Artificial Intelligence: A State-of-the-art Review.
content.abstract:
Purpose

This study aims to elucidate the expanding role of artificial intelligence (AI) in the early diagnosis of corneal and ocular surface diseases. AI has the potential to enhance diagnostic precision, streamline clinical workflows, and facilitate disease detection before clinical manifestations become evident.

Methods

A narrative literature review was conducted to assess the impact of AI and machine learning in corneal disease preclinical diagnosis. A comprehensive search in PubMed was performed using key terms such as "artificial intelligence," "machine learning," "deep learning," "corneal diseases," and "early diagnosis." Eligible studies were those published in English over the last decade that focused on AI-driven diagnostic approaches and prognostic modeling. Case reports, nonoriginal studies, and those with minimal AI integration were excluded. Data extraction emphasized AI methodologies, imaging techniques, diagnostic performance metrics, and clinical relevance.

Results

AI-powered machine learning models analyze vast imaging datasets, detecting subclinical abnormalities imperceptible to conventional diagnostic methods. This capability is particularly significant in early keratoconus detection, dystrophies, infectious keratitis, conjunctival neoplasia, and other corneal pathologies such as dry eye or Steven-Johnson disease, where subtle morphological changes precede clinically apparent disease.

Conclusions

The integration of AI into corneal disease diagnostics and management could mark in the future a transformative shift in Ophthalmology, offering precision, efficiency, and scalability. By facilitating early disease detection and individualized patient assessments, AI minimizes diagnostic inconsistencies and accelerates clinical decision making. Continuous algorithm refinement and real-world validation are crucial to maximizing AI's clinical utility. To fully harness AI's potential, multidisciplinary collaboration among ophthalmologists, data scientists, and regulatory bodies is imperative to address standardization, ethical concerns, and implementation barriers. As AI-driven technologies continue to evolve, they will redefine the standard of care in corneal disease diagnosis, therapeutic precision, and patient outcomes.

records.title: Deep Learning-Based Retinal Vascular Analysis with Quantitative Metrics for Hypertensive Microvascular Damage.

content.title: Deep Learning-Based Retinal Vascular Analysis with Quantitative Metrics for Hypertensive Microvascular Damage.
content.abstract: Background/Objectives: The goal of this study was to determine whether deep learning (DL)-assisted retinal vascular analysis detects subclinical microvascular remodeling associated with hypertension-mediated target organ damage (TOD) in patients with absent or mild hypertensive retinopathy (HR). Methods: This prospective study included age-comparable hypertensive patients with TOD (n = 54), hypertensive patients without TOD (n = 54), and healthy controls (n = 54). Color fundus photographs underwent DL-based segmentation using the Retinal Microvascular Health Assessment System, ophthalmologist quality review, and Fiji morphometric analysis. Central retinal arteriolar and venular equivalents (CRAE and CRVE), arteriovenous ratio (AVR), and arterial and venous network metrics were quantified. Results: AVR decreased progressively from 0.814 ± 0.038 in controls to 0.740 ± 0.043 in hypertensive patients without TOD and 0.655 ± 0.042 in those with TOD (p < 0.001). CRAE and CRVE differed among groups (p < 0.001 and p = 0.002). Arterial fractal dimension and vessel area density (VAD) declined stepwise (both p < 0.001), whereas arterial skeletonized vascular density (SVD) and diameter were primarily reduced in TOD. Venous VAD and diameter differed (p = 0.022 and p = 0.006), but venous SVD did not (p = 0.146). After adjustment among hypertensive participants, TOD remained associated with lower AVR, CRAE, and all arterial network metrics except tortuosity (all p < 0.001), but not with venous parameters. Conclusions: Retinal arterial alterations were associated with established extra-retinal TOD in patients with absent or mild HR. Residual cardiovascular confounding limits interpretation, and longitudinal studies are needed to establish temporal relationships, predictive value, and clinical utility.

records.title: Modeling distinct pathogenesis of early- and late-onset preeclampsia via hierarchical representation learning of interactome.

content.title: Modeling distinct pathogenesis of early- and late-onset preeclampsia via hierarchical representation learning of interactome.
content.abstract:
Objectives

We developed and validated the pathogenesis models by hierarchical representation learning of interactomes connecting endometrial maturation, placentation, chorioamnionitis, and hemolysis, elevated liver enzyme, and low platelet (HELLP) syndrome.

Methods

We utilized 19 gene sets from our previous work to infer interactomes to develop (n = 177) and validate (n = 352) explainable artificial intelligence models for each preeclampsia subtype using deep-insight visible neural network, gradient-weighted class activation mapping, and large language model.

Results

The hierarchically learned representations identified novel genes for late-onset preeclampsia (LOPE), similar to chorioamnionitis (ANKRD13A, SLA), and HELLP syndrome (PDE5A). We also identified novel genes for early-onset preeclampsia (EOPE), similar to HELLP syndrome (SWAP70, GREM2, GPR146, PIP5K1B, EZR).

Conclusions

Our pathogenesis models connected HELLP syndrome with both LOPE and EOPE. However, chorioamnionitis was only connected with LOPE.

records.title: The association between large language model dependence and academic anxiety among nursing students: statistical indirect associations through artificial intelligence addiction and academic burnout.

content.title: The association between large language model dependence and academic anxiety among nursing students: statistical indirect associations through artificial intelligence addiction and academic burnout.
content.abstract:
Background

Increasing use of large language models in nursing education has raised questions about the association between reliance on these tools and academic distress. This study examined direct and specific indirect associations between large language model dependence (LMD) and academic anxiety (AA) through artificial intelligence addiction (AIA) and academic burnout (AB).

Methods

A cross-sectional survey was conducted from March to April 2026 among 473 nursing students in Guangdong Province, China, including students undertaking clinical placements. The four constructs were assessed using items selected from published self-report instruments. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was performed with age and sex included as covariates. Direct and specific indirect associations were evaluated using bootstrapping with 5,000 resamples.

Results

Cronbach's α ranged from 0.914 to 0.944, composite reliability from 0.935 to 0.954, and average variance extracted from 0.560 to 0.721. Heterotrait-monotrait ratios ranged from 0.485 to 0.733, supporting discriminant validity. Model fit evidence was mixed: SRMR was 0.068, whereas NFI was 0.812, below the 0.90 reference value. The model explained 49.2% of the variance in academic anxiety. Large language model dependence showed a small positive direct association with academic anxiety (β = 0.138, 95% CI [0.006, 0.278], p = 0.048). Significant specific indirect associations were identified through academic burnout (β = 0.205, 95% CI [0.123, 0.303]) and through artificial intelligence addiction followed by academic burnout (β = 0.098, 95% CI [0.049, 0.147]); both p < 0.001.

Conclusion

Large language model dependence was positively associated with academic anxiety among nursing students, with specific indirect associations through academic burnout and through artificial intelligence addiction followed by academic burnout. These findings highlight the relevance of problematic AI use and study-related exhaustion to academic distress. However, the cross-sectional design does not establish temporal ordering or causal mediation.

records.title: Retinal Artificial Intelligence Reclassifies SCORE2-Based Cardiovascular Risk Across the ESC/EAS Statin-Indication Boundary: A UK Biobank Prospective Cohort Study.

content.title: Retinal Artificial Intelligence Reclassifies SCORE2-Based Cardiovascular Risk Across the ESC/EAS Statin-Indication Boundary: A UK Biobank Prospective Cohort Study.
content.abstract:
Aims

Whether a retinal artificial intelligence (AI) risk score reclassifies SCORE2 cardiovascular risk stratification in statin-naive adults across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary is uncertain. We evaluated the retinal AI risk score for 10-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) prediction.

Methods

In 40,672 statin-naive UK Biobank participants (aged 40-69, without diabetes), cardiovascular risk categories and treatment recommendation status (Class I or IIa vs neither) were defined using the 2025 ESC/EAS focused-update framework. Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) adjusted for SCORE2 or for established risk factors. The incremental predictive value of adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 was evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation.

Results

Over a 10.0-year median follow-up (914 ASCVD events), the very high retinal AI risk group independently predicted ASCVD (SCORE2-adjusted HR 2.32 vs low risk; p<0.001). Adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 reclassified risk across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary (statin-eligibility NRI [net reclassification improvement] 0.012, p<0.001); reclassification was statistically significant but modest (continuous NRI 0.445, p<0.001), without C-index or net-benefit gain. In the statin-indicated subgroup, retinal AI risk groups further stratified risk (SCORE2-adjusted HR 2.16; p<0.001). Statin-not-indicated participants in the high or very high retinal AI risk groups had numerically similar observed 10-year risk to all statin-indicated, untreated participants (p=0.758). There was no evidence of effect modification by clinically detectable retinal disorder (interaction p=0.93). Incremental value was greater in women than men (sex interaction p<0.001).

Conclusion

Adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 produced modest bidirectional risk reclassification across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary; these findings warrant prospective validation.Abstract word count: 250 words.

records.title: Deep Learning-Based Automated Detection, Segmentation, and Quantification of Retinal Fluid on Optical Coherence Tomography: A Validation Study.

content.title: Deep Learning-Based Automated Detection, Segmentation, and Quantification of Retinal Fluid on Optical Coherence Tomography: A Validation Study.
content.abstract: Objectives: To validate a deep learning-based algorithm for automated detection, segmentation, and quantitative assessment of retinal fluid on optical coherence tomography (OCT) across multiple retinal diseases. Methods: In this retrospective validation study, spectral-domain OCT volume scans from eyes with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD), diabetic macular edema (DME), and macular telangiectasia type 2 (MacTel) were analyzed. Automated segmentation was performed using the fluid analyzer on Skopix by NetraMind Innovations, a deep learning-based framework trained to identify intraretinal fluid (IRF), subretinal fluid (SRF), pigment epithelial detachment (PED), and subretinal hyperreflective material (SHRM). Automated segmentations were reviewed and manually corrected by two masked experienced retina graders, with discrepancies adjudicated by a senior retina specialist. Scan-level detection performance was evaluated using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), and Gwet's first-order agreement coefficient (AC1). Spatial segmentation agreement across all B-scans was assessed using the Dice coefficient. Quantitative agreement between automated and manually corrected fluid volumes was evaluated using correlation and Bland-Altman analyses. Inter-grader reliability was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). Results: A total of 98 OCT volumes comprising 31 nAMD, 25 DME, and 42 MacTel eyes were included. In nAMD, IRF detection demonstrated a sensitivity of 81.8%, specificity of 83.0%, and AUC of 0.876, while SRF demonstrated a sensitivity of 81.4%, specificity of 96.7%, and AUC of 0.901. In DME, sensitivity, specificity, and AUC were 99.6%, 97.3%, and 0.989 for IRF and 98.4%, 96.4%, and 0.978 for SRF, respectively. In MacTel, IRF demonstrated a sensitivity of 87.3%, specificity of 95.1%, and AUC of 0.927, while SRF demonstrated a sensitivity of 86.8%, specificity of 98.4%, and AUC of 0.929. Segmentation agreement between automated and manually corrected annotations was high across disease groups, with Dice coefficients of 0.829 and 0.922 for IRF and SRF in nAMD, 0.858 and 0.941 in DME, and 0.908 and 0.97 in MacTel, respectively. Automated fluid volumes demonstrated strong correlations with manually corrected measurements, with minimal systematic bias on Bland-Altman analysis. Conclusions: The automated segmentation algorithm demonstrated strong validation performance for the detection and quantitative assessment of retinal fluid across nAMD, DME, and MacTel. High segmentation agreement, particularly for IRF and SRF, and strong volumetric agreement with expert-corrected measurements support the potential use of automated OCT fluid quantification in clinical practice and research.

records.title: Association between deep-learning-derived retinal aging speed and rapid decline of renal function in the Japanese general population.

content.title: Association between deep-learning-derived retinal aging speed and rapid decline of renal function in the Japanese general population.
content.abstract:
Background

The eye and the kidney share microvascular features, and retinal changes have been postulated to reflect systemic cardiometabolic dysfunction. Recently, retinal age, estimated by deep learning (DL) from a single fundus photograph, has been shown to predict cardiovascular events. The present study aimed to determine whether retinal aging speed, defined as the individual-specific annual rate of change in DL-estimated retinal age, is associated with rapid estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) decline.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed the longitudinal data obtained from 7807 Japanese individuals who underwent repeated health check-ups with serial measurements of eGFR and fundus photographs (median 9.0 visits over median 8.0 years). We evaluated the relationship between retinal aging speed during the baseline period (from baseline to year 4) and rapid eGFR decline (≤ -3 ml/min/1.73 m²/year) during the follow-up period (after year 4).

Results

The incidence of rapid eGFR decline was significantly higher in the highest quartile of retinal aging speed than in the lowest quartile as the reference group in the fully adjusted model adjusting age, sex, body mass index, blood pressure, diabetes, smoking, eGFR, and proteinuria [odds ratio (OR) 1.34; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.06-1.68; P = .015]. In the multivariable logistic regression models, retinal aging speed was associated with rapid eGFR decline after adjusting multiple key confounders (OR 1.14; 95% CI 1.02-1.29; P = .027).

Conclusions

Taken together, DL-derived retinal aging speed is independently associated with rapid eGFR decline in the Japanese general population.

records.title: Global research trends of artificial intelligence in echocardiography (1984-2025): a bibliometric analysis.

content.title: Global research trends of artificial intelligence in echocardiography (1984-2025): a bibliometric analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Echocardiography has evolved substantially since its introduction in 1954. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers transformative potential for image acquisition, quantification, interpretation, and reporting. Despite growing research interest, a comprehensive evaluation of the historical trends and evolution of AI in echocardiography is lacking. The study aimed to conduct a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of the global research landscape in this field.

Methods

A systematic literature search was conducted using the Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection databases for publications on AI in echocardiography from inception through November 10, 2025; no language filter was applied. Data analysis was performed using Microsoft Excel, Microsoft Access, and IBM SPSS Statistics. In addition, bibliometric mapping and data visualization were conducted.

Results

Overall, 2682 publications received 35,083 citations (mean, 13.08 citations per publication), spanning 1984-2025. Original articles, conference papers, and review articles accounted for 87.4% and 98.5% of total publications and citations, respectively. Publication output remained limited until approximately 2015, rose gradually thereafter, and accelerated markedly after 2018, with similar output in 2024 and 2025. The United States led in both publication volume and total citations, followed by China and the United Kingdom. The United States also had the highest collaboration link strength, and seven of the top 10 institutions were in North America (six in the United States and one in Canada). Mayo Clinic ranked first, with 142 publications and 3604 citations, and had the earliest first indexed publication among the top institutions (1992). The journal JACC: Cardiovascular Imaging ranked first in both total citations (1,911) and citations per publication (36.75). "Echocardiography," "deep learning," "artificial intelligence," and "machine learning" were the most frequently used terms. The thematic evolution showed continuity of algorithmic-centric themes (1984-2019) with emerging clinically oriented themes (2020-2025).

Conclusions

This comprehensive bibliometric analysis highlights the rapid expansion of AI research in echocardiography, characterized by an accelerating publication output and emerging clinically oriented research topics. These findings reflect growing research interest in integrating AI into echocardiographic practice and highlight the need for future research prioritizing multicenter validation, clinical translation, and equitable real-world implementation.

records.title: Beyond scales: Artificial intelligence, language, and behavior in suicide risk modeling-a narrative review.
records.publisher: European neuropsychopharmacology : the journal of the European College of Neuropsychopharmacology

content.title: Beyond scales: Artificial intelligence, language, and behavior in suicide risk modeling-a narrative review.
content.abstract: Suicide is a leading, preventable cause of premature mortality, yet identifying individuals at imminent risk remains difficult. There are no validated biomarkers for routine stratification, and common approaches (clinical interviews, rating scales, self-report) are limited by subjectivity, reporting bias, and weak positive predictive value for rare outcomes. Rapid advances in artificial intelligence (AI)-including machine learning, deep learning, and large language models-offer opportunities to integrate heterogeneous signals relevant to risk and treatment response. This narrative review summarizes recent AI-enabled prediction and characterization of suicidal thoughts and behaviors across major data modalities: structured electronic health records and claims; natural language processing of clinical notes and digital text; speech and facial/behavioral signals; neuroimaging and other neurobiological measures; and passive sensing from smartphones and wearables. We review common modeling and evaluation practices, emphasizing clinically relevant performance assessment (discrimination and calibration) and the importance of temporal and external validation. We also highlight barriers to translation, including class imbalance and label noise, dataset shift across sites and time, limited prospective evaluation, and the need for interpretable outputs that can support medication decisions and care pathways (e.g., triage, monitoring, and stepped interventions). Ethical and implementation challenges-privacy and consent, algorithmic bias and equity, governance, and the clinical consequences of false-positive and false-negative predictions-are discussed with an emphasis on safe deployment. We conclude with priorities for the field, including multimodal longitudinal cohorts, harmonized reporting standards, and pragmatic trials to determine whether AI decision support measurably improves suicide-prevention outcomes.

records.title: Empirical Evaluation of Post Hoc Interpretability Methods for Clinical Trust in Deep Learning Diagnostics.

content.title: Empirical Evaluation of Post Hoc Interpretability Methods for Clinical Trust in Deep Learning Diagnostics.
content.abstract: Background/Objectives: Brain tumor classification from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has been significantly improved through deep learning techniques; however, the lack of interpretability remains a major challenge for clinical adoption. Methods: This study proposes an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI)-driven framework for multiclass brain tumor classification using a baseline convolutional neural network (CNN) and four transfer learning models, namely ResNet50, DenseNet121, MobileNetV2, and EfficientNetB0. The models were trained and evaluated on a publicly available brain MRI dataset consisting of glioma, meningioma, and pituitary tumor classes. Their classification performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC), and confusion matrix analysis. To enhance transparency and interpretability, Grad-CAM, LIME, and SHAP were used to visualize and quantify the regions contributing to the classification decisions. Results: Experimental results state that the transfer learning models consistently outperformed the CNN by learning more discriminative feature representations while producing more localized and interpretable explanations. The agreement among Grad-CAM, LIME, and SHAP confirms that the proposed models predominantly relied on tumor regions rather than irrelevant background information, thereby improving the interpretability and reliability of the diagnostic predictions. Conclusions: The proposed framework provides an effective and explainable computer-aided diagnosis system that supports trustworthy deep learning-based brain tumor classification and has the potential for decision-making.

records.title: Application of an Artificial Intelligence Simulated Patient Model in Teaching Neurosurgical Decision-Making.

content.title: Application of an Artificial Intelligence Simulated Patient Model in Teaching Neurosurgical Decision-Making.
content.abstract:
Aim

Training in neurosurgical decision-making remains a challenging component of standardized residency training. Traditional teaching models are limited in their ability to simulate the uncertainty and complexity encountered in real-world clinical scenarios. As a novel educational tool, the potential value of artificial intelligence (AI)-simulated patient models in surgical decision-making training requires further evaluation. This study aimed to explore the application of an AI-simulated patient model in neurosurgical decision-making education and to assess its effectiveness in improving residents' clinical decision-making abilities.

Methods

A retrospective study was conducted involving 157 residents who underwent standardized residency training in the Department of Neurosurgery from January 2023 to April 2026. Based on the implementation of the AI-simulated teaching model beginning in January 2025, participants were divided into two groups according to the teaching model used: an experimental group (n = 72, receiving AI-simulated patient teaching from January 2025 to April 2026) and a control group (n = 85, receiving traditional case discussion teaching from January 2023 to December 2024). The experimental group used a large language model-based virtual patient system powered by DeepSeek to perform dialogue-driven history taking, image interpretation, surgical planning, and risk prediction with real-time feedback, while the control group received conventional methods. After teaching, an objective structured clinical examination (OSCE) was used to assess surgical decision-making across five dimensions, including localization diagnosis, surgical approach, risk identification, emergency management, and surgical timing, and a questionnaire was used to measure teaching satisfaction.

Results

The total score for surgical decision-making ability was significantly higher in the experimental group than in the control group (p < 0.001). Dimensional analysis showed that localization diagnosis, surgical method selection, risk identification, emergency response, and surgical timing judgment were higher in the experimental group than in the control group (all p < 0.05). The excellent rate for each assessment dimension (>85 points) was significantly higher in the experimental group than in the control group (p < 0.05). The satisfaction score was also higher in the experimental group than in the control group (p < 0.001).

Conclusions

The AI-simulated patient model based on a general-purpose large language model was associated with better surgical decision-making performance among neurosurgery residents. It has significant advantages in localization diagnosis, surgical approach selection, risk identification, emergency response, and judgment of surgical timing, and is well accepted by residents.

records.title: Impact of Image Bit Depth Reduction on Deep Learning Performance in Chest Radiograph Analysis: A Multi-institutional Study.

content.title: Impact of Image Bit Depth Reduction on Deep Learning Performance in Chest Radiograph Analysis: A Multi-institutional Study.
content.abstract:
Rationale and objectives

Medical imaging typically generates 12-bit to 16-bit formats, yet conversion to 8-bit is often required. While deep learning has been widely explored in medical imaging, the influence of image bit depth on model performance is not fully understood. This study evaluates the impact of conversion from 16-bit to 8-bit for sex, age, and obesity classification using deep learning.

Materials and methods

In this retrospective, multi-institutional study, we analyzed 100,002 chest radiographs from 48,047 participants across three institutions. Images were uniformly quantized from the fixed 0-65535 range to 256 levels (0-255) with no additional processing. Three convolutional neural network architectures (ResNet52, EfficientNetB2, and ConvNeXtSmall) were trained on both 16-bit and 8-bit versions of the images. Model performance was evaluated using internal test datasets, randomly split multiple times, and an external test dataset. Statistical analysis included paired comparisons of area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) values, with Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons.

Results

Across all architectures and classification tasks, differences between 16-bit and 8-bit model performance were minimal (mean differences ranging from -0.218%-0.184%). Statistical analyses revealed no significant differences in AUC-ROC values between bit depths for any model-task combination (all p values > 0.05 after Bonferroni correction). Effect sizes were small to moderate (Cohen's d ranging from -0.415-0.391).

Conclusion

No statistically significant differences were detected between models trained on 16-bit and 8-bit images in the three evaluated tasks. These findings suggest that conversion to 8-bit images may reduce data storage requirements and improve data processing efficiency. Further research is needed to assess their usefulness in clinical tasks.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Treatment, and Perioperative Management: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence in Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Treatment, and Perioperative Management: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives.
content.abstract:
Background

Breast cancer is the most frequently diagnosed malignancy in women globally, accounting for approximately 2.30 million new cases and 666,103 deaths in 2022. Artificial intelligence technologies including machine learning, deep learning, radiomics, and natural language processing have been widely applied across the breast cancer care continuum. However, no systematic review restricted to primary studies with patient-level or image-level data has synthesized evidence spanning all clinical domains simultaneously.

Objectives

To evaluate the performance, methodological quality, and clinical relevance of artificial intelligence primary studies across screening and diagnostic imaging, digital pathology, radiomics, perioperative management, prognostic prediction, and natural language processing in breast cancer.

Methods

PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from January 2015 to May 2026. Eligibility was restricted to original primary research reporting patient-level or image-level data; secondary syntheses were explicitly excluded. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2 and PROBAST. Reporting followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines.

Results

Of 5,275 identified records, 17 primary studies met eligibility criteria. In screening mammography (seven studies; n = 7,540 to 144,231 examinations), deep learning achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.876 to 0.939; a randomised trial in 80,033 women demonstrated non-inferiority to double reading with a 44.3% reduction in radiologist workload. In digital pathology (five studies; 270 to 44,732 whole-slide images), deep learning achieved AUC 0.985 to 0.994, exceeding unassisted pathologist performance in lymph node metastasis detection. Magnetic resonance imaging radiomics predicted pathological complete response in HER2-positive breast cancer with AUC 0.80. No breast cancer-specific perioperative primary study met the eligibility criteria. Deep survival networks achieved concordance index 0.626 versus 0.612 for Cox regression in breast cancer cohorts. Natural language processing identified metastatic recurrence in breast cancer clinical records with sensitivity 83% and specificity 73%. Risk of bias was low to moderate for imaging and pathology studies and high for small sample radiomics studies. Density-stratified performance was reported by only two imaging studies, and receptor status prediction from haematoxylin and eosin staining had not been validated as a safe alternative to immunohistochemistry.

Conclusions

Artificial intelligence demonstrated clinically meaningful performance across the five domains with eligible primary studies. Breast cancer-specific perioperative and intensive care primary studies were absent, representing the largest evidence gap. External validation, demographic diversity, and prospective clinical integration evidence remained the most consistently identified limitations. Prediction of molecular receptor status without immunohistochemistry requires rigorous prospective safety validation before it can complement standard testing.

records.title: Digital twin oncology and multi-omics-driven artificial intelligence models for personalized drug response prediction: A systematic survey of emerging computational paradigms and clinical implementation challenges.

content.title: Digital twin oncology and multi-omics-driven artificial intelligence models for personalized drug response prediction: A systematic survey of emerging computational paradigms and clinical implementation challenges.
content.abstract: The increasing complexity of tumor heterogeneity and variable therapeutic response has intensified the need for accurate personalized drug response prediction in oncology. Traditional trial-and-error chemotherapy strategies often result in suboptimal outcomes, toxicity, and delayed therapeutic adjustments. Rapid advances in multi-omics technologies, artificial intelligence (AI) and digital twin modeling have significantly reshaped computational oncology research. This survey systematically reviews peer-reviewed research and review articles published from 2021 onward that investigate emerging computational paradigms integrating digital twins and multi-omics AI for drug response prediction. The foundational concepts in digital twin oncology, multi-omics profiling and AI-driven precision medicine are outlined initially. The existing approaches are categorized into four major paradigms such as omics-driven machine learning models, deep learning based multimodal architectures, mechanistic digital twin simulation frameworks and hybrid digital twin AI systems enabling adaptive therapy optimization. The multi-omics data integration strategies, including early, intermediate, late, network-based and graph/pathway-based fusion techniques. The survey synthesizes recent developments in drug sensitivity prediction, immunotherapy response modeling, tumor evolution forecasting and virtual clinical trials, while critically analyzing challenges related to data heterogeneity, interpretability, generalization, privacy, regulatory compliance and ethical considerations. Finally, future directions are highlighted such as real-time adaptive digital twins, federated learning, explainable AI and regulatory ready clinical deployment frameworks. Overall, this review provides a structured taxonomy, comparative analysis and research roadmap for advancing integrated digital twin and multi omics AI systems toward clinically actionable precision oncology.

records.title: Artificial intelligence analysis of oral mucosal lesions in white-light clinical photographs: A systematic review of visual features and validation.

content.title: Artificial intelligence analysis of oral mucosal lesions in white-light clinical photographs: A systematic review of visual features and validation.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to conventional oral photographs for recognition, classification, localization, segmentation, and risk assessment of oral mucosal lesions. This systematic review evaluated how clinically relevant visual information-including color, texture, morphology, borders, and spatial patterns-is represented by AI systems and assessed performance, validation, explainability, human comparison, and clinical translation. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched for studies directly analyzing conventional white-light clinical photographs. Risk of bias was assessed with PROBAST + AI, and certainty with Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation-based approaches. Fifty-three studies were included, 30 published in 2025-2026. Forty-six used implicit deep-learning visual representations, three multimodal vision-language models, two explicit color analyses, and two explicit texture analyses. Thirty-one studies primarily addressed image-level diagnostic classification/recognition, 15 spatial detection/localization or lesion delineation, six screening/triage/referral or biopsy-oriented decision support, and one longitudinal malignant-transformation prediction. Six used independent external cohorts and five compared AI with human readers. Methodological concerns were frequent, no sufficiently coherent group supported meta-analysis, and certainty remained limited across evidence bodies. Current evidence therefore supports technical feasibility rather than established clinical effectiveness, with translation requiring stronger patient-level independence, external validation, prospective multicenter evaluation, and evidence of clinical benefit.

records.title: Is Large Language Model a New Hope for the Global South? A Rapid Bibliometric Synthesis of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education.

content.title: Is Large Language Model a New Hope for the Global South? A Rapid Bibliometric Synthesis of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), especially the recent proliferation of generative Large Language Models (LLMs), is transforming traditional anatomy education by introducing new teaching tools. However, the adoption of these cutting-edge technologies raises questions about global educational equity. It remains unclear whether AI will serve as a digital equalizer or further exacerbate marginalization. This rapid bibliometric synthesis aims to provide a comprehensive, data-driven overview of the "Application of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education" (AAAE). We seek to map the intellectual landscape, detect structural and technological shifts, evaluate the geopolitical disparities, and provide corresponding references. A total of 85 consolidated records were retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus. These data constituted the whole panorama of AAAE. Bibliometrix and CiteSpace were utilized for static and dynamic mapping. A multidisciplinary expert panel validated the thematic clusters using Gwet's AC1 and the Normalized Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI). Publications surged following ChatGPT's release, indicating a shift from specialized computer vision to the application of general-purpose LLMs. While high-income countries maintain leadership, AI could exert a "democratizing effect" on upper-middle-income countries, doubling their odds of publication compared to traditional anatomy. Six research frontiers and three research trajectories were captured, and corresponding implications for future researchers in the global south and north were presented. AAAE could be conducted using a stratified strategy: different expansions of AI technologies for pedagogy; leveraging commercial APIs to bypass infrastructure bottlenecks; and validating open-source models. Global equity critically demands cross-border collaboration and inclusive datasets.

records.title: Efficacy and safety of linaclotide plus polyethylene glycol for bowel preparation before colonoscopy in elderly Chinese patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Efficacy and safety of linaclotide plus polyethylene glycol for bowel preparation before colonoscopy in elderly Chinese patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Elderly adults often have inadequate bowel preparation and poor tolerance to high-volume polyethylene glycol (PEG). Linaclotide may enhance intestinal secretion and transit. We compared linaclotide plus PEG (Lin + PEG) with PEG alone in elderly adults.

Methods

We searched CBM, CNKI, VIP, Chinese Medical Journals Full-text Database, Wanfang, PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science from inception to April 23, 2026, for randomized controlled trials comparing Lin + PEG with PEG alone in Chinese adults aged ≥60 years, or trials reporting extractable elderly subgroup data. Two authors independently screened studies and extracted data. Risk of bias was assessed using Version 2 of the Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials (RoB 2). Meta-analysis was performed using Review Manager and Stata. Prespecified subgroup analyses were conducted according to constipation status, linaclotide dose, and PEG-volume comparability.

Results

Twelve RCTs conducted in China, involving 1,334 participants, were included. Lin + PEG improved total bowel cleansing quality [MD = 0.93, 95% CI (0.66-1.20), p < 0.00001; I2 = 86%] and segmental BBPS scores. Lin + PEG was also associated with lower risks of vomiting [RR = 0.60, 95% CI (0.41-0.86), p = 0.006; I2 = 0%], abdominal pain [RR = 0.57, 95% CI (0.34-0.94), p = 0.03; I2 = 10%], abdominal distension [RR = 0.61, 95% CI (0.38-0.98), p = 0.04; I2 = 50%], and nausea [RR = 0.59, 95% CI (0.38-0.92), p = 0.02; I2 = 32%]. No significant difference was observed for total adverse events [RR = 0.76, 95% CI (0.57-1.01), p = 0.06; I2 = 60%]. Lin + PEG also reduced total procedure time [MD = -2.35 min, 95% CI (-3.11 to -1.60), p < 0.00001; I2 = 68%]. The polyp detection rate (PDR) was higher in the Lin + PEG group [RR = 1.25, 95% CI (1.01-1.55), p = 0.04; I2 = 47%].

Conclusion

In elderly Chinese adults, Lin + PEG may improve bowel cleansing and reduce total procedure time. No clear increase in reported adverse events was observed, although the certainty of the safety evidence remains limited.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251183002, identifier (CRD420251183002).

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Cervical Cytology: Opportunities and Limitations in Screening, Triage, and Diagnostic Support.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence in Cervical Cytology: Opportunities and Limitations in Screening, Triage, and Diagnostic Support.
content.abstract: Cervical cancer remains a major global health challenge, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, where access to screening, vaccination, and timely treatment may be limited. Cervical cytology has played an important historical role in prevention, but it is labor-intensive, time-consuming, and subject to observer variability and limited sensitivity. In many contemporary screening programs, HPV testing is now used as the primary screening test, while cytology is used mainly for the triage of HPV-positive women. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning (DL), has shown considerable potential in medical image analysis and computer-aided diagnosis. This review summarizes current applications of AI in cervical cytology and related diagnostic workflows, including automated and assisted slide screening, liquid-based cytology, the triage of equivocal or HPV-positive cases, and colposcopy support. Across these settings, AI-assisted systems may improve efficiency, standardization, and diagnostic consistency, and may reduce workload in resource-constrained environments. However, the evidence is heterogeneous, and important challenges remain, including the need for large and diverse datasets, prospective validation, regulatory approval, digital infrastructure, workflow integration, and the resolution of ethical and legal issues. AI should therefore be regarded as a promising adjunct to human expertise rather than a replacement in cervical cytology and related clinical diagnostic pathways.

records.title: How accurate is AI in detecting marginal jaw bone loss? A systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: How accurate is AI in detecting marginal jaw bone loss? A systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Objective

Detecting marginal jaw bone loss on radiographs is crucial for diagnosing periodontitis but remains difficult and time-consuming. This review evaluated artificial intelligence (AI) accuracy in identifying the alveolar bone crest and estimating bone loss compared with dental professionals. Moreover, we also assessed whether AI models can detect changes in bone levels over time.

Methods

We conducted a systematic review in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines, with diagnostic accuracy as the primary outcome. The review protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42024517330). Searches were performed in PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane, and Scopus up to August 2025. Two independent reviewers screened the articles at the abstract and title levels, and performed full-text and risk-of-bias assessments. A qualitative synthesis was complemented by a random-effects meta-analysis of studies reporting binary classification of marginal bone loss.

Results

Sixty-four studies met the inclusion criteria, with 16 included in the meta-analysis. AI models demonstrated promising performance in detecting the alveolar bone crest and showed high diagnostic accuracy for marginal bone loss, with a pooled sensitivity of 92.3 %, a specificity of 91.7 %, and an AUC of 0.97. However, high heterogeneity and frequent risk of bias were identified. No study evaluated changes in bone levels over time or was performed in a clinical setting.

Conclusion

AI holds promise for facilitating diagnostic decision-making in periodontal care. However, its clinical utility remains limited due to methodological issues. Future research should emphasize external validation, diverse datasets, and longitudinal image analysis to better align AI tools with real-world diagnostic needs.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence for Thyroid Nodule Diagnosis: From Multimodal Integration to Clinical Utility.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence for Thyroid Nodule Diagnosis: From Multimodal Integration to Clinical Utility.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) for thyroid nodules should be evaluated against the decisions it changes, not diagnostic accuracy alone. This critical narrative review examines ultrasound, cytology, histology, and molecular models and distinguishes modality-specific prediction from implemented multimodal learning. The original PubMed/MEDLINE search through 10 August 2026 was supplemented on 25 September 2026 by targeted OpenAlex searches and checks of primary publications, reporting standards, and regulatory sources. Selected studies are compared by sample size, reference standard, acquisition setting, testing design, and performance with confidence intervals where available. We explain feature concatenation, intermediate representation learning, cross-attention, and decision-level fusion, and examine whether integration improves on the strongest component. Reported gains are inconsistent, and complete-case multimodal datasets may exclude the low-risk nodules most relevant to avoiding biopsy. High discrimination for histological malignancy or occult nodal disease does not demonstrate reduced overdiagnosis, fewer operations, or improved survival. A thyroid-specific translation roadmap therefore addresses active surveillance, partial verification and spectrum bias, Hashimoto thyroiditis and multinodular disease, cytology preparation shifts, category-specific thresholds, operator dependence, reporting frameworks, and regulatory change control. The priority is a calibrated, externally tested tool using information available at a defined clinical decision, followed by prospective evaluation of patient and workflow outcomes. A unified imaging-pathology-omics system and reliable AI prediction of surveillance progression remain research objectives rather than established clinical capabilities.

records.title: Choriocapillaris Dysfunction in Retinal Diseases: Multimodal Imaging Biomarkers, Pathophysiological Insights, and Emerging Clinical Applications.

content.title: Choriocapillaris Dysfunction in Retinal Diseases: Multimodal Imaging Biomarkers, Pathophysiological Insights, and Emerging Clinical Applications.
content.abstract: The choriocapillaris is the terminal capillary bed that sustains the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and the outer retina, and its integrity is inseparable from that of the RPE-Bruch's membrane complex it supplies. Histopathological work established decades ago that choriocapillaris density declines with age and falls further in disease, but for most of that period, the layer could not be assessed reliably in living eyes. Optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA), particularly with swept-source instrumentation, signal compensation and validated thresholding, has changed this: choriocapillaris flow deficits can now be quantified reproducibly and followed over time. A flow deficit is, however, a signal-level measurement that does not by itself establish anatomical capillary loss, and this distinction is maintained throughout. This review examines what that capability has revealed. We first summarize choriocapillaris anatomy, its functional coupling to the RPE through polarized vascular endothelial growth factor secretion, and the mechanisms implicated in its failure, including complement-mediated endothelial injury, Bruch's membrane thickening, oxidative stress and venous overload. We then address the methodology in detail-slab definition, shadow compensation, binarization, averaging and the artefacts that inflate or mask flow deficits-because the comparability of published values depends almost entirely on these choices. The clinical sections review choriocapillaris involvement in age-related macular degeneration, where baseline flow impairment has been associated with subsequent drusen formation and with the rate of geographic atrophy enlargement, an association that is temporal rather than proven causal and that rests on a small number of cohorts; in the pachychoroid spectrum, where the layer is thought to be compressed rather than primarily diseased; and in diabetic retinopathy, myopia, inherited retinal dystrophies, inflammatory chorioretinopathies and systemic vascular disease. We conclude by considering structure-function relationships with outer retinal integrity and visual sensitivity, the relevance of choriocapillaris metrics as trial endpoints and stratification variables in the complement inhibitor era, and the standardization, validation and automation required before these biomarkers can be used in individual patients.

records.title: Association of fermented dairy consumption with asthma and wheeze risk in children: a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies.

content.title: Association of fermented dairy consumption with asthma and wheeze risk in children: a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies.
content.abstract:
Objective

This study aimed to systematically assess the association between fermented dairy consumption and the risk of asthma and wheeze in children.

Methods

Following a protocol registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251269745), a systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library up to January 2026 to identify observational studies reporting relevant effect estimates. A random-effects model was used to pool odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Subgroup analyses were performed based on study design, outcome phenotype, product type, and timing of exposure. Sensitivity analyses, including Hartung-Knapp adjustment, were conducted to assess robustness.

Results

A total of 11 studies (119,372 participants) were included. In the primary DerSimonian-Laird random-effects analysis, fermented dairy consumption was associated with a reduced risk of the composite outcome of asthma/wheeze in children (OR = 0.72, 95% CI: 0.55-0.95), with substantial heterogeneity (I 2 = 77.0%). However, this association was not retained after Hartung-Knapp adjustment (OR = 0.72, 95% CI: 0.52-1.01; p = 0.054). Subgroup analyses indicated that this association was largely influenced by cross-sectional studies (OR = 0.51, 95% CI: 0.33-0.78), whereas no statistically significant association was found in cohort studies (OR = 0.91, 95% CI: 0.72-1.16). Additional subgroup analyses showed stratum-specific differences, but tests for subgroup differences were not statistically significant. Egger's test did not indicate statistically significant publication bias. The overall certainty of evidence was very low.

Conclusion

The current evidence does not support a robust association between fermented dairy consumption and the risk of asthma or wheeze in children. The observed potential association may be influenced by methodological factors, particularly study design. Well-designed, large-scale prospective studies are warranted to further clarify this association.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251269745, identifier: CRD420251269745.

records.title: Can live microbial interventions support healthy aging? A systematic review and meta-analysis of cognitive and muscle outcomes in aging adults.

content.title: Can live microbial interventions support healthy aging? A systematic review and meta-analysis of cognitive and muscle outcomes in aging adults.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Preserving cognitive and physical function is central to healthy aging, and the gut microbiota may influence both brain and muscle physiology. We evaluated whether live microorganism-based interventions affect cognitive and muscle-related outcomes in aging adults.

Methods

We systematically reviewed randomized placebo-controlled trials of probiotics, synbiotics, or fecal microbiota transplantation in populations with a mean age of at least 60 years. MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched. Random-effects meta-analyses used Hedges' g when at least three studies or independent comparisons reported sufficiently comparable outcomes. The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251065993; https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251065993).

Results

Twenty-four trials involving 1,809 participants were included qualitatively: 20 evaluated cognitive outcomes and four evaluated muscle-related outcomes. Eleven unique studies contributed to at least one meta-analysis. For Mini-Mental State Examination scores, the overall pooled estimate was positive (g = 1.02; 95% CI: 0.36-1.68; I 2 = 90.84%). In exploratory post hoc subgroup analyses, the estimate was positive in Alzheimer's disease (g = 1.46; 95% CI: 1.14-1.79) but not statistically significant in broader cognitive impairment (g = 0.49; 95% CI: -0.78 to 1.77); the subgroup difference was not significant (p = 0.15). Excluding both Akhgarjand et al. intervention arms yielded a positive estimate in Alzheimer's disease (g = 1.63; 95% CI: 1.21-2.06), although only two studies remained. The pooled Repeatable Battery for the Assessment of Neuropsychological Status result was not statistically significant (g = 0.46; 95% CI: -0.50 to 1.41). Handgrip strength showed a modest positive estimate (g = 0.46; 95% CI: 0.06-0.85), but exclusion of Qaisar et al. attenuated it to non-significance (g = 0.23; 95% CI: -0.27 to 0.73).

Discussion

Live microorganism-based interventions showed preliminary short-term functional signals, but the small evidence base, high cognitive heterogeneity, short follow-up, and sensitivity to individual studies preclude firm efficacy conclusions. Subgroup and two-study sensitivity findings are exploratory. No eligible fecal microbiota transplantation trial was identified, so the evidence derives exclusively from probiotic and synbiotic studies.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251065993, unique identifier: CRD420251065993.

records.title: Comparison of drug regimens for recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.

content.title: Comparison of drug regimens for recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Cervical cancer is one of the most common cancers among women worldwide. For patients with recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer (R/MCC) after surgery or radiotherapy, drug therapy is the primary treatment modality. Currently, head-to-head comparison studies of different immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI) combination regimens are lacking in clinical practice. This study aims to provide an indirect comparison of the relative efficacy of various drug regimens (including chemotherapy, targeted therapy, and immunotherapy) for R/MCC patients through a systematic review and network meta-analysis (NMA).

Method

The study adhered to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analyses (PRISMA) reporting guidelines and systematically searched databases including PubMed, Web of Science, Embase and the Cochrane Library for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing drug treatment regimens. The primary efficacy endpoint was overall survival (OS). Progression-free survival (PFS) was analyzed as a secondary endpoint to provide additional evidence of clinical activity. We conducted the NMA using a Bayesian random-effects model, estimated the ranking of each treatment regimen via the Surface Under the Cumulative Ranking Curve (SUCRA), and performed a Frequentist NMA as a sensitivity analysis.

Result

A total of 15 RCTs involving 4,588 R/MCC patients were included. The NMA results for OS showed that ICI combination regimens (with or without bevacizumab) provided a significant benefit compared to backbone chemotherapy. Specifically, the regimen of pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy and bevacizumab showed the greatest potential for OS benefit (Frequentist HR: 0.45, 95%CI: 0.30-0.67 vs. cisplatin plus paclitaxel), ranking first by SUCRA (87%). Among traditional chemotherapy regimens, only the cisplatin plus paclitaxel regimen was significantly superior to single-agent cisplatin (Frequentist HR: 0.74, 95%CI: 0.59-0.93). The NMA results for PFS indicated that the cadonilimab plus chemotherapy regimen was the most outstanding (Frequentist HR: 0.46, 95%CI: 0.32-0.66 vs. cisplatin plus paclitaxel), ranking first by SUCRA (90%). The rankings of the treatment regimens were consistent across both Bayesian and Frequentist, suggesting strong robustness of the results.

Conclusion

ICI combination regimens (with or without bevacizumab) are likely the optimal choice for treating R/MCC patients. Pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy and bevacizumab is most likely to yield the OS benefit, and cisplatin plus paclitaxel remains the best backbone chemotherapy regimen for R/MCC. This study provides comprehensive indirect comparison evidence for clinicians in selecting R/MCC treatment strategies.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251180897, identifier CRD42024604107.

records.title: A systematic review of non-contact medical IoT systems for physiological biomarker monitoring.

content.title: A systematic review of non-contact medical IoT systems for physiological biomarker monitoring.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Non-contact medical Internet of Things systems measure physiological biomarkers such as heart rate (HR), respiration rate (RR), temperature, oxygen saturation (SpO₂), and blood pressure (BP) without physical contact with the patient. These systems combine sensing modalities including cameras, radar, Wi-Fi, acoustic, and infrared sensors with signal processing and learning algorithms to deliver comfortable, non-invasive monitoring. Prior reviews have largely examined individual sensing modalities or signal processing techniques in isolation, leaving cross-modality system architecture and privacy-preserving design underexamined.

Methods

We conducted a systematic review following PRISMA guidelines and analyzed 88 recent studies of non-contact monitoring systems. Studies were characterized by sensing modality, system architecture, target physiological parameter, validation setting, and reported performance. We additionally assessed each study for methodological quality and examined the extent to which privacy-preserving mechanisms were incorporated into system design.

Results

Radar and vision-based systems dominate the corpus, together accounting for approximately three-quarters of included studies, while sound, Wi-Fi, embedded sensor, and mixed-modality designs remain at an earlier stage of validation. Research effort is heavily concentrated on two parameters: RR appears in 83% of studies and HR in 67%, while no other parameter exceeds 11%. BP, SpO₂, and temperature therefore remain largely unaddressed by contactless methods. Heterogeneous reporting metrics across studies prevent direct statistical comparison of performance between modalities.

Discussion

The findings indicate that modality selection should be driven by deployment context rather than headline accuracy. Radar suits wards and intensive care units where patients are covered or moving, vision and sound suit structured clinical spaces with stable conditions, embedded sensor designs suit eldercare beds and chairs, and mixed radar and vision systems suit precision-critical settings such as neonatal and postoperative monitoring. Persistent challenges include signal reliability in uncontrolled environments, limited benchmarking due to the absence of standardized datasets, privacy and ethical concerns, and poor integration with existing healthcare infrastructure. Building on these insights, we propose a conceptual federated, edge-based learning framework, presented as a design proposal for future implementation rather than a validated system, and outline research directions to accelerate clinical translation.
